content_voiceover: This slide continues the rhabdomyosarcoma discussion by defining favorable versus unfavorable primary tumor sites, which is one of the key inputs into risk stratification alongside stage, histology, and resectability. Favorable sites include the orbit, the head and neck excluding parameningeal locations, the genitourinary tract excluding the bladder and prostate, and the biliary tract. These sites tend to be more accessible for complete resection or respond well to combined therapy, and they carry a better prognosis. Unfavorable sites include the bladder and prostate, the extremities, cranial parameningeal locations, meaning sites near the skull base and meninges where local extension into the central nervous system is a real risk, and a catch-all other category that includes the trunk and retroperitoneum. Recognizing which bucket a given primary site falls into is essential for boards, because site is one of the factors used directly in risk group assignment and treatment intensity.
keypoints: Favorable sites: orbit, head and neck excluding parameningeal, nonbladder/nonprostate genitourinary tract, biliary tract
Unfavorable sites: bladder and prostate, extremity, cranial parameningeal, trunk and retroperitoneum
Cranial parameningeal sites carry risk of direct CNS extension
Primary site is a key input into RMS risk stratification
keypoint_voiceover: For RMS, favorable sites are orbit, nonparameningeal head and neck, nonbladder nonprostate genitourinary tract, and biliary tract. Unfavorable sites are bladder and prostate, extremity, cranial parameningeal, and trunk or retroperitoneum, and site feeds directly into risk stratification.
